sonnet.q1: The scheduler's 02:00 UTC trigger starts attempt 1. It extracts all columns of `orders` rows from the Postgres read replica where `updated_at` is later than `window_start` (hwm minus 2 hours).
sonnet.q2: A bulk import can be stamped up to 90 minutes before its row becomes visible. Because of that, each night re-reads a 2-hour lookback before the watermark.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps `updated_at`. The next nightly extract picks it up (window is updated_at later than hwm minus 2h), and the MERGE updates the warehouse row because src.updated_at is greater than tgt.updated_at.
sonnet.q4: The app never hard-deletes. A delete sets `deleted_at`, which bumps `updated_at`, so the normal window picks it up. The order stays in warehouse `orders` with `is_deleted = true`.
sonnet.q5: ROLLBACK, the error is logged to `run_log`, hwm is unchanged, and the lock is released if this run holds it. If it was attempt 3, on-call is paged. Otherwise the plan checks whether this run_id already committed. If it did, the run counts as a success. If not, the next attempt starts 15 minutes after this one ended. An attempt still running at its deadline is stopped and counts as failed.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the last committed night, since they read only committed rows. The 06:00 watchdog posts a staleness alert to the data-alerts channel, with the attempt count and last error. The on-call is also paged if the third attempt failed.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. For each creation day in the last 30 days it compares count and checksum on both sides, and reloads any mismatched day, extracting rows created that day and applying the same MERGE.
sonnet.q8: Staged rows are deduplicated per `order_id` keeping the greatest `updated_at`. The MERGE updates a matched row only when `src.updated_at > tgt.updated_at`. Equal `updated_at` is a no-op.
sonnet.q9: It is stored in `etl_control.watermark` in the warehouse. The value is greatest(old hwm, max `updated_at` over the extracted rows), written together with the run_id and commit time. This happens in the same transaction as the merge, just before COMMIT. If the extract is empty, the value stays the same.
sonnet.q10: The merge and watermark update happen in one transaction that commits all at once. Dashboards read only committed rows, so they never see a half-loaded night. If the warehouse lacks multi-statement transactions, a shadow table is swapped in atomically instead.
sonnet.q11: Each attempt has its own staging table `stg_orders_<run_id>`, so a retry never reuses a partial load. The failed attempt's staging is dropped if a staging check or replica error failed it. Orphaned staging tables older than a few days are swept. The retry extracts from the same unchanged hwm, window_start = hwm minus 2 hours.
sonnet.q12: It re-reads rows whose `created_at` falls within that UTC day, from the replica. They are staged and applied with the same MERGE rule in the reload's own transaction. Nothing is deleted. The nightly watermark is not changed.
